page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance from the Dadsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes a bundled local storage capacity of 2835 GB on NVMe SSDs and is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core processing, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests. It also achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and image and text processing. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing fall into the top 25% bracket. Memory performance is strong, with read-only small block bandwidth and large block write bandwidth in the top 25%, though large block read-only bandwidth drops to average levels.

For database and application workloads, the instance shows strong capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which can leverage the fast local NVMe SSD storage. It also handles small-scale LLM inference efficiently, reaching top-tier speeds for 135M parameter models, though medium 7B model prompt processing is average. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it is not suited for heavy deep learning training or large-scale model inference. The instance offers high resource density and a balanced compute-to-memory ratio, making it a cost-efficient choice for enterprise web serving, database hosting, and software development pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 4.0 GB per core, and includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers top-tier single-core and multi-core CPU performance, alongside strong memory bandwidth and database processing capabilities. While it lacks a GPU, its high-speed local storage and robust CPU performance make it highly efficient for workloads such as database hosting, static web serving, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
